svg.title: claudia computes — rotating objects on a sheet
svg.desc: A sheet with an arrow and a note turned about their centres while staying anchored to their cells; how rows moving above them affects them; the handle when there is no room above; a reminder that turned text in cells is a different thing.
svg.text: claudia computes — turning an object that lives on a sheet

For review before any code. Content is invented. The shared parts (handle, Format ▸ Rotate, Rotate By…) are mock-up 1. A sheet object hangs from a cell (E6.17, CellAnchor) and a turn never changes that.
A · Turning an arrow on a sheet
The arrow and the note hang from their cells (D12, E13). Turning moves neither: the anchor cell stays, the object turns about its own centre.
B · A row is inserted above
The anchor is the cell, not a pixel position: the object moves down with its cell,
keeps its turn and its size, and never leaps (E6.17).
after Edit ▸ Row ▸ Insert Above on row 3
Whatever happens to the rows and columns around it, the turn is not touched.
C · When there is no room above
An object at the top of the visible grid would put its handle under the column
headers (or the frozen rows). Then the stem and handle go below the object.
Same rule in composes, where an object can sit at the top of the page area. In creates
the slide has a margin all round, so it never applies.
The handle and chip of mock-up 1. A sheet object is turned about the centre of its frame; the frame's top-left stays on the anchor cell.
The anchor cell is outlined while an object is held, with a pin at the frame's top-left corner and a chip naming the cell. The dashed grey square is the
frame as if it were upright.
The arrow lies over the cells; the cells beneath it are not changed by it, and the turn does not move the anchor.
A note turned 354°: the same entries, the same history; a viewer sees it turned and cannot move it.
The arrow points at the total in C10 and the note says why. The model does not link the two; named relations between objects are on the list (“every object
Not this: turned text inside a cell (an angled column heading) is a cell style, “text direction”, and has no handle; it belongs to the cell styles (E6.13).
People will look for it under Rotate, so Format ▸ Rotate stays greyed on a cell.
Open points, with a recommendation each
Recommended: a chart does not turn (axes at an angle are hard to read). Rotate is
greyed for it; pictures, shapes, text boxes and rendered text do turn.
Recommended: Edit ▸ Select Next Object, Ctrl+Alt+Shift+B, in composes and computes;
Esc returns to the cell. Without it the handle is for mouse users only.
Proposed: an object that a frozen row or column covers is cut at the pane, like the
cells; its handle follows rule C. To check against how objects behave under frozen
